source_title: Where to Buy Tickets to Golden State Valkyries vs. Atlanta Dream
source_excerpt:

For the first time in the history of the WNBA Finals, there will be a Game 7. The Atlanta Dream decisively beat the Golden State Valkyries during a midday game at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena, taking the lead within the first minute and holding onto it until the final whistle to force a seven-game series.
At a Glance: Where to Buy Tickets to Valkyries vs. Dream
General sale: Ticketmaster (10:00 a.m. PT)
Resale: SeatGeek , StubHub , VividSeats , GameTime
Watch Live: USA (Watch with DirecTV Free trial ); Peacock
The final will take place at San Francisco’s Chase Center, and the Valkyries will now hope that the energy of Ballhalla can carry them to their first title — which would be a remarkable run for a team that’s only in its second season. The game is set for 5:00 p.m. PT (8:00 p.m. ET) and airs on USA and streams on Peacock .
The Dream’s Game 6 performance was powered in part by Angel Reese , who notched a double-double and set a new record for most rebounds in a WNBA finals series. But teamwork made the Dream work; four of Atlanta’s players scored in the double digits, compared to just two for the Valkyries.
Game 6 was mired by scheduling conflicts, which meant tip-off was 12:30 p.m. ET on a weekday due to the Hawks-Cavaliers game taking place the same day. Still, the game took place in front of a packed arena.
Where to Get Tickets to Valkyries vs. Dream
Unsurprisingly, tickets for Game 7, which falls on Halloween, are pricey. Stubs start at just under $400 for upper sections, while floor seats start at around $5,900. General sale and resale tickets are available from Ticketmaster . General sale is 10:00 a.m. PT, Oct. 30.
Fans can also check resale sites, which sometimes have lower prices and discounts. These are a few options, and how much fans can expect to pay.
A single ticket starts at just over $400 for the game, while courtside seats will set you back over $5,000.
Tickets are a little pricier on StubHub compared to SeatGeek, with 200-level seats running around $450. 100-level seats start at around $830.
Tickets on VividSeats start at around $400, while 100-level seats are available starting at around $700.
Sport-focused ticketing site GameTime has tickets available starting at just under $400, while 100-level seats start at around $800.
